newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to supply emergency funds to Hanbo suppliers.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to supply emergency funds to Hanbo suppliers.

text.p: South Korea's Finance Ministry said in a statement the central bank will supply emergency operating funds to subcontractors and suppliers of the debt-ridden Hanbo Steel Corp, a ministry statement said.
It did not say how much the funds would be.

"Emergency operating funds will be supplied to small- and medium-sized companies expected to face financial difficulties because of Hanbo default," the statement said. The firms could also delay repayment of bank loans. No details were given.

The central bank will the manage money supply flexibly to minimise the adverse effects of Hanbo's failure. "The central bank will ease fears of tight liquidity in the short-term money market through Repo arrangements," it said.
It said the bank will increase the money supply ahead of the lunar New Year holidays, a traditional money spending season, which falls on February 7-9.
Hanbo said it would file for court receivership on Friday after defaulting on payments of more than five billion won worth of promissory notes on Thursday.
The ministry said Hanbo faced financial trouble after investing heavily in a steel mill with capacity of six million tonnes a year.
Hanbo officials said the steelmaker was saddled with debt totalling 5.7 trillion won.
